But (1) repository code does handle berserk in research: research/b3_population_expertise/src/clock.py `def berserked(clocks, base_seconds)` ("A berserked arena game keeps the `180+0` header and starts at 90 seconds") and ingest.py:223 `if berserked(...): self._drop("berserk or impossible starting clock")`; DATA_PROTOCOL.md rule 'not berserk'. The scratchpad score_games.py also halves `init_side` for the berserking colour and zeroes its increment. Only shared/pgn-clock.ts and scripts/build_account_corpus.ts (the product/owner path) lack handling. (2) Scope: shared/pgn-clock.ts secondsSpentAt uses clockTimes[ply−2]; clockMsRemainingAt uses clockTimes[ply−2]; both return null for ply<2. Index 0 (header base) is read only at ply 2 (Black's first move). Ply 3 reads clockTimes[1], a real post-move reading. So only owner-as-Black berserk games are affected (frozen_2209.ndjson: owner berserk as White 84, as Black 62), only at ply 2, and ply-2 positions are almost always excluded as book. '146 games' and 'ply 2/3' overstate the defect.

errors.statement: Admissible feature 'opponentClockMsRemaining; clockBalanceMs; clockShare': "Derivable but NEVER written to any evidence row or scored corpus".
errors.what_source_says: shared/import-diagnostic.ts ImportedDecision carries `opponentClockMsRemaining: number | null` (line 98) and `timeControl: TimeControlMs` (line 116), and decisionsFromGame fills both on every scored decision (lines 374-376: `opponentClockMsRemaining: clocks ? opponentClockMsRemainingAt(game.clockTimes, ply) : null`). They are absent only from the evidence dump: scripts/run_account_prereg.ts rows (lines ~117-131) write playerId, gameId, ply, phase, secondsTaken, clockMsRemaining, cpLoss, accurate, standing, forced, book, speed. 'Never written to any evidence row' is true; 'or scored corpus' is not — the in-memory scored corpus carries them.

Known only at commit'; (b) `standing`, `eval_trend_2ply` (mover_rel(i) − mover_rel(i−2), engine evals), `own_prev_wp_loss`, `own_errors_so_far`, `plies_since_own_error` sit in VOCAB_OBS ('player-observable') although they are engine-derived — GATE-CUE-PLAYER-OBSERVABLE (scripts/cue-scan.ts: 'a quantity that exists only because a program scored a position') would reject them as cues; `own_prev_wp_loss`/`own_errors_so_far` are lagged copies of the target inside the same game; (c) score_games.py sets `spent_cs = 0` for ply < 2 and own_before = full base at ply < 2, where the product returns null (import-diagnostic.ts: 'every imported game with clocks contributed at least one invented "0 seconds" decision, and 0 < 45'); common.eligible() requires seconds.notna(), so a 0 passes; (d) research engine is Stockfish 17.1 native MultiPV 3, not the shipped SF18 Lite WASM MultiPV 1 (ENGINE_PARITY 13.61% flips) — the ledger records this but no parity re-check has run.

CANONICAL TARGET DEFECT documented in docs/MEASUREMENTS.md ('NOT FIXED HERE: the same defect on the import path ... the mating move of every imported game that ended in mate is still scored as a blunder') and confirmed live on scripts/sf-wasm.sh (`info depth 0 score mate 0`, `bestmove (none)`): 507 owner-won-by-mate games in the frozen window → 507 eligible decisions labelled inaccurate by construction. shared/pgn-clock.ts opponentClockMsRemainingAt(ply 1) reads clockTimes[0] = header base, which is wrong by half whenever the OPPONENT berserked (279 − 146 = 133 games where only the opponent berserked, plus games where both did); this affects every derived clockShare/clockBalanceMs at the owner's ply-1 decision as White. Not mentioned.

The mission ledger's baseline uses `gap12`, `n_near`, `ambiguity_entropy`, `edge` (MultiPV ≥ 2 quantities) — the synthesis states these are 'NOT available from the owner's existing MultiPV-1 depth-12 run; population-only today'; they are now available for the owner from the SF 17.1 MultiPV-3 scratchpad run, but under a different instrument than the canonical labels (R-03 pooling refusal applies within the mission's own table: engine features and the canonical `accurate` come from different engines unless the WASM re-score is used for the target).

research/b3_population_expertise/src/clock.py `berserked()` and DATA_PROTOCOL.md 'not berserk' rule are a repository precedent (drop the game) for the berserk fix the synthesis says has no owner; the lowest-layer repair choice (halve base for the berserking side, as scratchpad score_games.py does, vs drop, as B3 does) is undecided.
